clue.text: Precipitous road — stick behind

blocks.note: a switch is a thin stick or cane
behind and back both mean at the rear

explanation.surface: A warning sign on a steep mountain road: keep to the rear of the car in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a road zigzagging up a steep slope, doubling back on itself at each hairpin bend.

clue.text: Successfully negotiate to get partners in to dine

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to sup is to have supper, to dine
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Arranging for one's companions to come to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South and East-West are the two partnerships, so partners can be a pair of compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To sew up a deal is to conclude it successfully, securing agreement on favourable terms.

clue.text: As Athenian orator, I executed philosopher

blocks.note: taken as written
the Athenian thinker condemned to death by hemlock

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek speaker confessing to having put a thinker to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Isocrates was a celebrated teacher of rhetoric and speechwriter in fourth-century BC Athens.

clue.text: The Duke of Gordon's finch

blocks.note: first meaning: the nickname of the Duke of Gordon, a Scottish nobleman
second meaning: a dialect name for the brambling, a northern finch

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it read as one bird owned by a duke; it is two separate meanings, his title and the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belonged to George Gordon, fifth Duke of Gordon, and is also a folk name for the brambling.

clue.text: Some support for Israeli character in Galilean village

definitions.note: Bethany is usually placed in Judea, near Jerusalem

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so one piece is placed below the other

blocks.note: beth is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet
some and any are both indefinite quantity words

explanation.surface: Some backing for an Israeli figure living in a village by the Sea of Galilee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a written letter, not a person. In a down entry the piece meaning 'some' supports, so sits below, the Hebrew letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethany is the New Testament village home of Lazarus, Martha and Mary, visited by Jesus.

clue.text: Dyestuff from crab due for processing

indicators.note: processing works raw material over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A colouring agent extracted from a crab that is ready for factory treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cudbear is a purple dye made from lichens, patented by an eighteenth-century Scottish chemist.

clue.text: Stay in the pack

blocks.note: first meaning: a support that holds something up
second meaning: a front-row forward in a rugby scrum, the pack

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the pack is the group of forwards who form the scrum; the props sit at either side of its front row.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is both a supporting beam or stay and a rugby forward position within the scrum's front row.

clue.text: The right house doctor to prescribe a lozenge

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
HO is the abbreviation for house
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: The proper in-house physician recommends a throat pastille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lozenge' suggests a medicinal sweet, but it is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb is a parallelogram with equal sides, the diamond figure also called a lozenge in geometry and heraldry.

clue.text: She promotes the construction of new sea-ports

definitions.note: a phrase describing the person, standing for a noun

indicators.note: construction builds something new, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman backing the building of new harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: A patroness is a female patron, a woman who sponsors and supports a cause or artist.

clue.text: Thirty days constantly at church? What a long time

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a period of thirty days in which every day is a churchgoing day
second meaning: an exclamation about something taking ages

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom; the question mark warns it is not a dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a very long period, as in 'not in a month of Sundays'.

clue.text: Deal perhaps with damaged illustration

blocks.note: deal is pine or fir timber, an example of wood
something cut has been damaged

explanation.surface: A card game where the cards dealt include a spoiled picture card.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal here is the timber, not the handing out of cards; 'perhaps' flags it as one example of a wider class.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a carved wooden block, used as a picture in books.

clue.text: Kick hippy, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: in rugby, a drop kick taken from the 22-metre line to restart play
second meaning: someone who has rejected conventional society, as hippies did

explanation.surface: Someone urging a long-haired hippy to be booted out.
explanation.definitionFit: A dropout abandons mainstream society or study, and the term was applied to sixties hippies; in rugby it is also a restarting kick.

clue.text: Part of book about crime in Framley house

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a page is one part of a book
arson is the crime of setting fire to property

explanation.surface: Pointing to a passage in a book describing a crime committed somewhere called Framley.
explanation.walkthrough: Framley Parsonage is a novel by Anthony Trollope, named after a vicar's house in the fictional village of Framley.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is a clergyman's residence; Trollope's novel title makes the one at Framley famous.

clue.text: Soldiers noisily disapprove of ban

blocks.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
to boo is to jeer loudly in disapproval

explanation.surface: Troops loudly objecting to a prohibition imposed on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social or religious prohibition, something strictly forbidden by custom.

clue.text: Persuade Italian to take severe criticism

blocks.note: to get someone to do something is to persuade them
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Trying to talk an Italian into accepting a harsh telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Get it' is an informal idiom for being punished or scolded, as in 'you'll get it when you're home'.

clue.text: Rows in the balcony very close to being clean, it's said

definitions.note: describes the answer's place in a proverb rather than meaning it

indicators.note: it's said asks for the sound of the words spoken, and also nods to a saying

blocks.note: the gods is the highest balcony in a theatre, and rows there are its lines

explanation.surface: Seats in a theatre's upper tier said to be almost spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'cleanliness is next to godliness', so the answer is very close to being clean. The gods is the theatre's top gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb puts it right next to cleanliness, so it is literally said to be very close to being clean.

clue.text: Long drink for a lady, rum with last of the lemonade

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of the word that follows
rum is old slang for odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of lemonade

explanation.surface: A bartender suggesting a lady's drink of rum topped with lemonade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit in the drink but is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is beer served in a glass about three feet tall, so it is literally a long drink.

clue.text: Stars in poorly done drama

indicators.note: poorly means badly, so the letters come out in a bad order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Famous actors appearing in a badly staged play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like the cast of the play but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a group of stars named after the princess of Greek myth.

clue.text: Girl's inclined to be fat

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, with the possessive s
tended means was inclined, leaned towards

explanation.surface: A remark that a girl has a tendency to put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Distended means swollen or bloated outward, as a stomach becomes, which fits fat as an adjective.

clue.text: No hope for Bunyan's giant

blocks.note: first meaning: a complete loss of hope
second meaning: the giant of Doubting Castle in The Pilgrim's Progress

explanation.surface: A hopeless outlook for a giant from an old story.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the absence of hope, and Giant Despair imprisons Christian in John Bunyan's allegory.

clue.text: Leather suits required by family

blocks.note: 'that does' means that suits or will serve
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Leather outfits a family insists on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' reads as clothing next to 'Leather' but is a verb meaning serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is soft leather made from the hide of a female deer, or sheep and lambskin finished similarly.

clue.text: Takes part on and off, maybe

blocks.note: first meaning: to side with someone, take their part in a dispute
second meaning: in cricket the field is split into the on side and the off side

explanation.surface: Someone who joins in only intermittently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On and off' reads as 'now and then' but names the two halves of a cricket field, either side of the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides is a verb for supporting one party in an argument and a plural noun for the halves of a pitch.

clue.text: Jones borrowing from Bernini? Goodness!

indicators.note: borrowing from means taking a run of letters directly out of the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the sculptor's name and the start of the exclamation

explanation.surface: A shocked reaction to an architect copying from the Italian baroque master Bernini.
explanation.walkthrough: BernINI GOodness. Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect, so the first name defines the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo is the forename of the English architect Jones, so the surname clues the first name by association.

clue.text: Very fat wife is divorced, in other words

indicators.note: divorced means separated, so this person is taken away from the rest

blocks.note: widest is the superlative of wide, so very fat
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A grossly overweight wife has split from her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from WIDEST. Id est is Latin, abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase meaning 'that is', used to restate or clarify, just like 'in other words'.

clue.text: Supporter at the back has tough assignment

blocks.note: stern means severe or tough
a post is a job or assignment

explanation.surface: A loyal backer stuck with a difficult job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but here it is a structural timber; 'at the back' is the stern of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sternpost is the upright timber at a ship's rear that carries the rudder, a support at the back.

clue.text: No real newspaperman took things lightly

blocks.note: a toy gun or toy car is not a real one
ED is short for editor, the newspaperman

explanation.surface: A fake journalist who didn't treat his work seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: To have toyed with something is to have treated it casually and without serious purpose.

clue.text: Choose artist to represent Agamemnon's daughter

blocks.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: Picking a painter to portray a figure from Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Electra was a child of King Agamemnon who helped avenge his murder.

clue.text: Extremely ratty after Jack's fraud

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its outer letters only
after says one piece follows the other in the answer

blocks.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards
the first and last letters of ratty

explanation.surface: Someone very annoyed after being cheated by a man called Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is dishonest, roguish behaviour, so trickery or fraud is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Block a burrow

blocks.note: first meaning: a rectangular paving stone
second meaning: a badger's underground home

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop up an animal's hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is both a squared granite paving stone and the network of tunnels where badgers live.

clue.text: Superb partnership has such an exciting finish

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes before finish in the phrase

blocks.note: grand means splendid or superb
in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batters

explanation.surface: A sporting pair whose excellent teamwork produces a thrilling climax.
explanation.walkthrough: A grandstand finish is a close, thrilling end to a contest, so the clue describes the phrase rather than the bare word.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandstand finish is one so tense it brings spectators in the main stand to their feet.
